dimensions.assessment: Affects all online ticket issuers, third-party service providers, consumers purchasing tickets online, and federal/state regulators and law enforcement agencies.
dimensions.evidence: Each online ticket issuer shall--establish, implement, and maintain an access control system, security measure

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new operational requirements, compliance procedures, reporting mandates, and substantial financial liabilities for violations.
dimensions.evidence: Any person who violates subsection (a) or (b) shall be liable for--a civil penalty of not less than $10,000 for each day

dimensions.assessment: Establishes civil monetary penalties and requires the FTC to create a publicly available consumer complaint website, but does not explicitly appropriate new federal spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of the Mitigating Automated Internet Networks for Event Ticketing Act, the Commission shall create a publicly available website

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016 by creating new mandates for ticket sellers, new FTC guidance and enforcement authorities, mandatory reporting, and law enforcement coordination.
dimensions.evidence: Section 2 of the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016 (15 U.S.C. 45c) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory requirements for ticket issuers alongside ongoing reporting and coordination duties.

missing_information: Exact figures on the total number of online ticket issuers or businesses affected.
Specific administrative cost estimates for the FTC to establish websites and reporting mechanisms.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill places new security, reporting, and safeguard requirements on online ticket issuers, broadens prohibitions against automated ticket-buying bots, establishes civil penalties of at least $10,000 per day for violations, and mandates law enforcement coordination and FTC reporting.

card.summary: The MAIN Event Ticketing Act expands federal measures to protect online ticket sales and consumer security by amending the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016. It prohibits the use of automated software to bypass ticket purchasing rules and access controls, requires online ticket sellers to implement specific security safeguards, mandates the reporting of circumvention incidents to the Federal Trade Commission, and establishes civil penalties and enforcement authorities.
